page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with 2 threads via hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 7.0 GB of system memory, matching a 3.5 GB per vCPU ratio, along with a shared 260 MB L3 cache. It includes no local storage devices, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence, and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX are supported at the instruction level.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate distinct contrasts between single-threaded and parallel processing on this configuration. The processor achieves solid single-core efficiency, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2081.0 and fast data transformation throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.12 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.36 GB/sec. However, because execution relies on only two virtual threads on a single execution core, multi-threaded capacity remains constrained. Geekbench multi-core registers at 2627.0, and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance falls into lower percentiles at 1888.09. Uncached memory throughput measures 15.64 GB/sec for reads and 10.00 GB/sec for writes across large blocks, reflecting memory subsystem constraints common to entry-tier virtual slices.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-2 delivers dedicated modern Intel execution cores suitable for lightweight server deployments without shared-core throttling. Due to its limited thread count and lack of onboard storage, it is unsuitable for heavy data compilation, intensive multi-threaded database transactions, or parallel analytics pipelines. Optimal workloads include lightweight web serving, microservices, background job workers, API endpoints, and low-scale caching tasks where consistent single-thread execution is required.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-2 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 7.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, the instance executes two threads across a single physical core and features hardware acceleration flags including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights strong single-thread efficiency, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2081.0 and 34.12 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics and memory throughput remain constrained due to the two-vCPU footprint, with uncached read speeds reaching 15.64 GB/sec and a multi-core Geekbench score of 2627.0. Qualitatively, the instance offers predictable dedicated execution for entry-level workloads. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, microservice hosting, routine background processing, and low-demand application development.
